name: Nail Polish & Acetone Remover
disposalSummary: Nail polish and acetone removers contain volatile flammable chemicals and cannot be poured down drains or tossed in standard trash.
stepByStepInstructions: Do NOT pour remaining polish down sinks or storm drains.
If the bottle is completely empty and dry, it can go into regular metal/glass/plastic recycling with the cap off.
If any liquid remains, take the bottle to a DSNY Special Waste Drop-Off Site or an upcoming SAFE Disposal event.
handlingTips: Ensure bottles are tightly sealed to prevent spills in transit.

name: Lithium-ion & Rechargeable Batteries
disposalSummary: Illegal to discard in trash in NYC. Lithium-ion batteries present severe thermal runaway fire risks in sanitation trucks and facilities.
stepByStepInstructions: Tape both contact terminals with clear packing tape or electrical tape, or place each battery into an individual plastic bag.
Never puncture, crush, or open damaged or swollen batteries.
Drop off at retail battery takeback locations (Best Buy, Staples, Home Depot) or DSNY Special Waste Drop-Off Sites.
handlingTips: NY State Rechargeable Battery Law requires retailers that sell rechargeable batteries to accept them back free of charge.

name: Alkaline Batteries (AA, AAA, C, D, 9V)
disposalSummary: Modern single-use alkaline batteries manufactured after 1996 contain no added mercury and are legal to put in regular household trash, though special drop-off is encouraged.
stepByStepInstructions: For 9V batteries, tape the terminals with clear tape to prevent sparking.
You can safely dispose of standard alkaline batteries in regular household trash.
Alternatively, bring them to a DSNY Special Waste Drop-Off Site for responsible metal recovery.
handlingTips: Be sure to double check that the battery is standard alkaline and NOT lithium or rechargeable before trashing.

name: Automotive & Lead-Acid Batteries
disposalSummary: Contains toxic lead and corrosive sulfuric acid. NYC law requires auto retailers and service stations to accept them back.
stepByStepInstructions: Keep upright and transport carefully in an acid-resistant container or heavy cardboard box.
Return to any store that sells car batteries (they are legally required to accept up to two batteries per month, and may refund your core deposit).
Or take to any DSNY Special Waste Drop-Off Site.
handlingTips: Never tip the battery on its side. Wear gloves if there is any visible corrosion.

name: Oil-Based Paint, Stains & Varnishes
disposalSummary: Classified as toxic and flammable hazardous waste. Cannot be put in curbside trash or poured down any sewer.
stepByStepInstructions: Keep in original labeled container if possible.
Do NOT allow to dry out indoors due to toxic fumes.
Deliver to a DSNY Special Waste Drop-Off Site or an official SAFE Disposal event.
handlingTips: DSNY limits drop-offs to up to five gallons per visit for NYC residents.

name: Latex & Water-Based Acrylic Paint
disposalSummary: Non-toxic latex paint can go in regular household trash ONLY AFTER being dried and hardened completely.
stepByStepInstructions: Remove the lid and stir in kitty litter, sand, or commercial paint hardener.
Leave in a well-ventilated area away from children and pets until rock solid.
Place hardened paint can with lid OFF in a double trash bag next to regular trash.
Or bring unopened/usable cans to DSNY Special Waste or PaintCare participating hardware stores.
handlingTips: Never discard liquid paint in the trash; sanitation trucks crush the cans and paint will spray across the street.

name: Motor Oil, Transmission & Brake Fluid
disposalSummary: Highly hazardous to waterways. Just one gallon of motor oil can contaminate one million gallons of fresh water.
stepByStepInstructions: Drain fluid into a clean, leakproof plastic jug with a secure cap.
Do NOT mix motor oil with water, gasoline, antifreeze, or solvents.
Any NY service station or quick lube that sells oil must accept up to 5 gallons per person per day free of charge.
Or bring to a DSNY Special Waste Drop-Off Site.
handlingTips: Proof of NYC residency (driver's license or utility bill) is required at DSNY sites.

name: Fluorescent Light Tubes & CFL Bulbs
disposalSummary: Contains toxic mercury vapor. Illegal to throw in household trash or recycling.
stepByStepInstructions: Wrap tubes or bulbs in newspaper or bubble wrap to prevent breakage.
Drop off at retail locations (such as Home Depot, Lowe's, or local hardware stores accepting CFLs).
Or bring to a DSNY Special Waste Drop-Off Site.
handlingTips: If a bulb breaks, ventilate the room for 15 minutes. Scoop up fragments with cardboard—do not vacuum.

name: Computers, Laptops, Tablets & Monitors
disposalSummary: NYS Electronic Equipment Recycling and Reuse Act bans all computers and monitors from disposal as trash.
stepByStepInstructions: Wipe personal data or remove the hard drive if privacy is a concern.
Drop off at any authorized electronics drop-off location (Best Buy, Staples, Salvation Army, Goodwill).
NYC residents in apartment buildings with 10+ units can also enroll in e-cycleNYC for free in-building collection.
Can also be dropped at any DSNY Special Waste Drop-Off Site.
handlingTips: Staples and Best Buy accept most computers and laptops regardless of brand or condition.

name: Televisions (CRT, LCD, OLED)
disposalSummary: Older CRT TVs contain up to 8 pounds of toxic lead. All TVs are strictly illegal to set out at the curb.
stepByStepInstructions: Drop off at municipal e-waste sites, participating Goodwill/Salvation Army drop-offs, or DSNY Special Waste sites.
Check with Best Buy before bringing extra-large TVs (some stores have screen size limits).
Or take to a seasonal SAFE Disposal event.
handlingTips: Do not attempt to break down or remove CRT glass tubes yourself due to implosion risk.

name: Cell Phones, Cables, Chargers & Keyboards
disposalSummary: Small electronics contain valuable copper, gold, and rare-earth metals that can be recycled.
stepByStepInstructions: Perform a factory reset to clear personal data.
Drop into e-waste bins at any Best Buy, Staples, or Apple Store.
Or bring to any of the 100+ partner drop-off locations across NYC.
handlingTips: Many wireless carriers also offer trade-in credits or donate functioning phones to charity.

name: Small Appliances (Toasters, Blenders, Microwaves)
disposalSummary: Appliances mostly made of metal/rigid plastic can go in curbside blue recycling bins, but e-waste partner drop-off is great for reuse.
stepByStepInstructions: Remove batteries or removable cords if applicable.
Small mostly-metal or rigid plastic appliances can actually go into your regular NYC Blue Bin (metal/glass/plastic curbside recycling).
Working appliances can also be donated to Goodwill or Salvation Army drop-off partners.
handlingTips: Do not confuse small appliances with refrigerators or air conditioners which require CFC Freon recovery appointments.

name: Air Conditioners, Refrigerators & Dehumidifiers
disposalSummary: Contains ozone-depleting refrigerants (CFCs / Freon). Requires an official DSNY Freon removal appointment before pickup.
stepByStepInstructions: Schedule a free CFC Recovery Appointment with DSNY at nyc.gov/dsny or by calling 311.
Place the unit curbside the evening BEFORE your scheduled appointment date with the doors removed or secured.
Once tagged by DSNY with an official green sticker, sanitation workers will collect it on your next recycling day.
handlingTips: Never cut refrigerant lines or attempt to vent freon gas yourself—it is dangerous and illegal.

name: Propane Tanks & Camping Gas Canisters
disposalSummary: Extreme explosion hazard. Never place any pressurized gas tank in curbside recycling or standard trash.
stepByStepInstructions: Standard 20-lb grill tanks can be exchanged or returned at hardware stores, Home Depot, or gas stations that participate in Blue Rhino or Amerigas tank exchanges.
Small camping fuel canisters (1-lb) can be brought to a DSNY Special Waste Drop-Off Site.
Never puncture pressurized tanks.
handlingTips: Transport tanks upright in a well-ventilated trunk or vehicle bed.

name: Smoke Detectors & Carbon Monoxide Alarms
disposalSummary: Ionization smoke alarms contain trace amounts of Americium-241 (radioactive isotope). DSNY permits regular trash disposal once battery is removed, or manufacturer mailback.
stepByStepInstructions: Remove the 9V or lithium backup battery and recycle the battery separately.
Check the back of the detector: if marked 'Ionization', you may mail it back to the manufacturer (address listed on the label).
DSNY allows non-battery smoke alarm bodies to be discarded in ordinary household trash if mail-back is unavailable.
handlingTips: Never disassemble the sealed ionization sensor chamber.

name: Pesticides, Weed Killers & Pool Chemicals
disposalSummary: Toxic chemicals are hazardous to sanitation workers, wildlife, and groundwater. They must be managed by specialized hazardous waste facilities.
stepByStepInstructions: Keep chemicals in their original containers with labels intact.
Never mix different chemical products together.
Bring directly to a DSNY Special Waste Drop-Off Site or an upcoming NYC SAFE Disposal event.
handlingTips: Limit of up to 5 gallons or 22 pounds per household per visit.
